questions.question:
Five students are standing in a line. Suman is standing next to Pranav but not next to Deena. Kumar is standing next to Raju, who is standing on the extreme left, and Deena is not standing next to Kumar.

Who is standing in the middle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**Meaning of Next to → के बगल में

Arranging them according to the given information,

1) Kumar is standing next to Raju, who is standing on the extreme left it means Kumar is standing next to Raju and Raju is standing on the extreme left.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afcf9d762bcba22babccfbfe4e5e5ef7fc96cf63d2dfad94e5ee69e391e51e66.png] 

2) Suman is standing next to Pranav but not next to Deena.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47bdef499f4abf97a1d069a362c5828c6ca81370af18a2ecef7ad65401667236.png] 

Suman is standing in the middle in the line.

Hence, **“Suman”** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

**"Who"** is used for the **second person** in a sentence.

For example,

Kumar is standing next to __**Raju, who**__ is standing on the extreme left → it means Kumar is standing next to Raju and Raju is standing on the extreme left. 

**"And"** is used for the **first person** in a sentence.

For example,

**Suman** is standing next to Pranav **but** not next to Deena → Suman is standing next to Pranav and Sumna is not next to Deena.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term.

11 : 169 :: 18 : .......
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is,

For 11 : 169,

11 + 2 = 13

13² = 169

Similarly,

18 : ….

18 + 2 = 20

20² = 400

So,

18 : **400**

‘400’ is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term.

Hence, “400” is the correct answer.

1, 3, 5, 11, 21, 43, 85, 171, .............
questions.solution:

3 × 2 – 1 = 5

5 × 2 + 1 = 11

21 × 2 + 1 = 43

85 × 2 + 1 = 171

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All scientists working in Japan are talented.

Some Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

**Conclusions:**

I. No Chinese scientist is talented.

II. Some talented Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

III. All talented scientists are Japanese.

IV. Some Chinese scientists are talented.

options.text: Only conclusion III and IV follow
Only conclusion II and IV follow.

questions.solution:
According to the given statements,

***Conclusion I:*** This does not follow, because it is mentioned in the statement that all the scientists working in Japan are talented, but it is not mentioned only Japanese people are talented.

***Conclusion II: ***This follow, because it is mentioned in the second statement that some Chinese scientists are also working in Japan.

***Conclusion III:*** This does not follow, because it is not mentioned in the statement that only Japanese are talented.

***Conclusion IV: ***This follows because some Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

Hence,** “only conclusion II and IV” follow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

 
• If there are two or more sentences that are used to frame a statement, then, the sentences must be interrelated, and mutual contradiction should be there.
 
• **Do not look for truthful notions. The information provided in the statement is the only requirement for a student to answer the question. No assumptions must be made.**
 
• Read the statement carefully and look for keywords that are common between the statement and the conclusions
 
• If there is more than one conclusion that is applicable to the statement, students must ensure that the conclusions they opt for have some relation with each other.

questions.question:
Five students took part in a cycling competition. Robert finished before Monish but behind Gunjan. Anil finished before Sunil but behind Monish.

Who won the competition?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

1) Robert finished before Monish but behind Gunjan → Gunjan > Robert > Monish

2) Anil finished before Sunil but behind Monish; → Monish > Anil > Sunil

The correct order is,

**Gunjan > Robert > Monish > Anil > Sunil**

Gunjan won the competition.

Hence, “Gunjan” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statements is true. even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:**

Some dolls are flowers.

No trees are dolls.

**Conclusions:**

I. No dolls are trees.

II. Some flowers are trees.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6bd0028526ee6eb0f8dd96d12e482f219a576a05a844da3f0f53e22a95f71462.png] 

Conclusion I: No dolls are trees → True (This is definitely true)

Conclusion II: Some flowers are trees → False (This is definitely false)

Hence, “only conclusion I” follows.
